newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana Land reserves rose, spending up.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana Land reserves rose, spending up.

text.p: Louisiana Land and Exploration Co on Tuesday said it replaced 131 percent of its 1996 worldwide production at a cost of $4.79 per barrel of oil equivalent.
It said that total excludes three successful wells drilled in Algeria in 1996 and a recent discovery well in Louisiana at South Fresh Water Bayou, where test results are pending.
The company also said its 1997 exploration budget, including seismic acquisition, currently stands at $178 million, up about 13 percent from 1996 spending.
Louisiana Land said its 1997 development budget stood at $62 million, for a combined exploration and development budget of $240 million.
Calling that total preliminary, Chief Executive H. Leighton Steward said: "We expect our capital budget to grow further as our 1997 program gets fully under way."

It said it would allocate about 76 percent of exploration dollars to domestic activities, primarily in south Louisiana and the Gulf of Mexico. Internationally, exploration activities are planned for Algeria, Venezuela, Colombia and Tunisia.

The company will spend 57 percent of the development budget on domestic projects, with the balance earmarked primarily for activities at the Thelma Fields in the North Sea and the KAKAP concession off Indonesia.
The company said it replaced 144 percent of domestic production at a cost of $4.99 per barrel of oil equivalent and 104 percent of international production at a cost of $4.19 per barrel.
It said toal reserves stood at 271.7 million barrels at the end of 1996, up 11.7 million from the end of 1995.

During 1996, worldwide reserve additions totaled 49.4 million barrels, with discoveries, extensions and revisions totaling 46.5 million. Domestic operations added 34.1 million barrels, while international operations added 12.4 million.
Louisiana Land said reserves purchased in 1996 totaled 2.9 million barrels.
